{{Short description|Mapping preserving identity}}{{No inline|date=May 2025}}
In [[abstract algebra]], a '''unital map''' on a [[C*-algebra]] is a map <math>\phi</math> which preserves the identity element:  

:<math>\phi ( I ) = I. </math>

This condition appears often in the context of [[completely positive map]]s, especially when they represent [[quantum operation]]s.  

If <math>\phi</math> is completely positive, it can always be represented as 

:<math>\phi ( \rho ) = \sum_i E_i \rho E_i^\dagger. </math>

(The <math>E_i</math> are the [[Kraus operator]]s associated with <math>\phi</math>).  In this case, the unital condition can be expressed as

:<math>\sum_i E_i E_i ^\dagger= I. </math>
